# Dansk Kemisortering A/S

> Danish company that sorts hazardous chemical waste (kemiaffald) on a modern,
> automated sorting plant — as an alternative to default incineration. We
> receive chemical waste from Danish recycling centers (genbrugspladser) and
> from industry, sort it, recycle packaging, and send chemical fractions to
> specialized treatment. The large majority of the sorted fractions are sold
> on to industrial companies.

## What we do

Standard practice in Denmark is to incinerate hazardous waste, including
sealed drums (spændelåsfade) with their contents. We sort instead:

1. **Receive** chemical waste from recycling centers and from industry
   (drums packed in vermiculite from the recycling centers).
2. **Sort** the products automatically: products pass through a scan zone with
   three cameras, where an AI model reads label, barcode and hazard marking and
   identifies the product halfway through the scan.
3. **Recycle** packaging materials where possible.
4. **Treat** chemical products through specialized processing, handled
   separately. The large majority of the fractions are sold on to industrial
   companies.

This is a circular-economy alternative to default incineration, designed to
be environmentally approved (miljøgodkendt), safe, and economically viable.

## Key facts

- Receives chemical waste from recycling centers and from industry.
- Automatic sorting with an AI model and three cameras on a conveyor belt.
- Operations are environmentally approved with high safety prioritization.
- Most sorted fractions are sold to industrial companies.
- Ongoing tests of recycling possibilities for plastic granulate.
- Can help with UN-approved sealed drums (spændelåsfade) and vermiculite.
